title: Trace Attribute Bridge and Anomaly Curator for Contextual SLO Alerting
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Current SLO and alerting surface lacks request-context continuity across traces, metrics and logs which leads to noisy burn-rate alerts and hard-to-triage incidents. This ticket implements a lightweight Trace Attribute Bridge (TAB) to propagate, persist and surface request attributes into metric/log pipelines and a downstream Anomaly Curator service that scores alerts with contextual signals to reduce false positives and improve paging decisions. Goal: reduce oncall noise by 30% for customer-facing latency/error SLOs while preserving time-to-detect. This work spans tracing hook updates, metric ingestion enrichment, log schema additions, anomaly scoring model, dashboard widgets and paging policy controls in Console.
acceptance_criteria: TAB is implemented in the tracing-hook library and emits sanitized attribute payloads for sampled and non-sampled traces
Metric ingestion pipeline accepts TAB payloads and attaches attributes to SLO time-series (no schema-breaking changes for existing metrics consumers)
Anomaly Curator service produces a per-alert contextual score and a recommended paging action (no-page, page-low, page-high)
Burn-rate alerts are gated by contextual score thresholds by default; oncall rotations receive 30% fewer pages in production canary region
New latency/error dashboard tiles show attribute-level SLO breakdowns and top correlated trace attributes
End-to-end synthetic test simulating burst + downstream degradation triggers proper burn-rate alert, curator scoring, and remediations via runbook links
All changes feature flagged and have a canary rollout plan with metrics to validate signal fidelity and latency overhead (<3ms p95 addition to trace sampling path)
Documentation and runbook updates present in confluence URL and linked from the alert definitions
implementation_notes: Trace hook changes: add compact TAB envelope that includes request_id, customer_tier, model_variant, route_id, sampled_kv_flags; ensure size <= 512 bytes and strip PII at source
Sampling policy: continue current sampling rates but attach non-sampled headers for lightweight TAB propagation; sample expansion during anomalies will enrich historical context

Metric pipeline: add an attribute-join stage in the ingestion cluster that consumes TAB payloads and writes attributes as labels to the SLO time-series in metrics-store; maintain cardinality controls via attribute allowlist and hashing for high-cardinality attributes
Log enrichment: update structured log schema to reference trace.request_id and include attribute references (not full payload) to avoid log bloat

Anomaly Curator: microservice that takes alert candidate, fetches recent traces and metrics for the SLO window, computes contextual features (route skew, model change, deployment tag, noise score) and returns a confidence score and recommended paging action
Scoring model: start with rule-based ensemble (weighted heuristics) and ship telemetry to evaluate candidate ML model later; rules configurable via Console
Dashboard: add attribute filter chips and heatmap widget showing SLO burn by attribute slices; link top trace samples for fast triage
Performance: aim for <50ms end-to-end Curator decision time for the majority of alerts; place Curator in same region as metric-evaluator to reduce RTT
Feature flags: split by component (trace-hook-enabled, metrics-attribute-join, curator-eval, paging-gating) to allow progressive rollout
Backwards compatibility: metrics consumers without attribute awareness should still receive time-series; attributes are optional labels
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: attribute cardinality explosion -> Mitigation: strict allowlist, hashing and cardinality caps with automatic fallback to aggregate buckets
Risk: increased latency on the hot path (trace hook) -> Mitigation: compact serialization, sampling-aware propagation, micro-benchmarks and p95 budget of 3ms
Risk: curator false negatives/mis-scorings -> Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds, manual override in Console, detailed audit logs for model decisions
Risk: accidental PII propagation -> Mitigation: central sanitizer in trace-hook library, automated tests and CI policy check for attribute allowlist
Risk: operational complexity for oncall -> Mitigation: phased rollout, training sessions, clear runbook entries, and a one-week hypercare with engineering on standby
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for trace-hook serialization + sanitizer
Integration tests for metrics-attribute-join using synthetic TAB payloads
End-to-end canary in staging region simulating multiple failure modes (backend slowdown, model degradation, network partition)
Smoke test: deploy feature flags off -> ensure no changes to existing alerts; turn on curator in read-only mode -> verify scores but no paging changes
A/B canary: 10% of traffic with full gating and 90% control; measure page volume, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), and false-positive rate
Load test: ensure metrics ingestion throughput with attributes at scale (target 10k attr-augmented points/s per ingestion shard)
Monitoring: new telemetry for TAB error rate, curator latency distribution, attribute cardinality metrics
rollout_plan: Week 1: merge trace-hook changes behind feature flag; unit/integration tests pass; deploy to staging
Week 2: enable metrics-attribute-join in staging; validate dashboards and no schema breakage; run synthetic tests
Week 3: deploy Anomaly Curator in read-only mode to production; collect scores for 48-72h and review with SREs and oncall leads
Week 4: enable paging gating in canary region (10% traffic); monitor page volume and MTTA; tune thresholds
Week 5: gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with 24h observation windows and rollback gates
Post-rollout: 1-week hypercare, retrospective and runbook updates
